title: Code Runner MCP Server -- T1059 unauthenticated run-code tool executes arbitrary source
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Detection for CVE-2026-5029 (cert.pl, 2026-05), affecting Code Runner
MCP Server "in all versions" -- no patch exists at authoring time.

When started with `--transport http`, the server exposes its `/mcp`
JSON-RPC endpoint on port 3088 with no authentication. An unauthenticated
remote caller can invoke the `run-code` MCP tool, supplying arbitrary
source code and a target language; the server executes it via
`child_process.exec()` using the corresponding language interpreter --
with the privileges of whatever user is running the MCP server process.
Unlike most rules in this corpus, there is no version cutoff to key a
negative case on: the source states this affects the project in all
versions and remains unfixed.

Detection logic flags a `tools/call` JSON-RPC request naming the
`run-code` tool arriving without an Authorization header -- the tool
name itself is the discriminator this vulnerable server exposes with no
gate at all, so its presence on the wire without credentials is the
vulnerability's exact trigger condition, not a heuristic approximation
of it.

Aggregated from 1 independent technical write-up (cert.pl, a
CERT-affiliated vulnerability coordination body). No patched version
exists -- operators should place this server behind an authenticating
reverse proxy or restrict network reachability until upstream ships a
fix, per the source's own recommendation.
